title: Make capture choices
summary: Separate motion, light, and rendered brightness.
outcomes: Compare two choices and explain the result instead of applying a universal style rule.
startingAssumptions: No camera or external service is required; all measurements and scenes here are fictional.
editorialRationale: Original two-beat unrelated course fixture proving content-driven teaching and stable identities.

concepts.definition: A way to compare how far the subject moves during the chosen exposure, separately from camera movement.
concepts.example: With unchanged aperture and scene, one eighth of the duration gathers one eighth of the light and gives the cyclist less time to travel.

concepts.definition: Change one factor while keeping the stated conditions fixed so the effect can be attributed to it.
concepts.example: The scene and aperture stay fixed. The interval changes.

questions.prompt: A tripod holds the camera still. The cyclist is blurred. What change directly reduces subject travel during exposure?

options.rationale: This gives the cyclist less time to move across the image.

options.text: Use a sturdier tripod at the same interval.
options.rationale: This may reduce camera shake, but does not reduce the cyclist’s travel.

questions.prompt: At fixed scene light and aperture, exposure changes from1/100 to1/200 second. What happens to captured light?

options.rationale: The capture interval halves under the stated fixed conditions.

options.text: It doubles when ISO is raised.
options.rationale: ISO can change signal gain or rendering; it does not itself admit more light.

beats.title: Separate subject motion from camera motion
beats.outcome: Make a reasoned choice and identify what evidence would change it.
beats.explanation: A cyclist can move while the camera stays still. Use a [[photo-m01-motion-concept|motion budget]] to reason about what crosses the frame during exposure. Shortening the interval reduces that travel; holding the camera steady solves a different problem. Decide whether you want frozen detail or a visible trail before choosing a duration.

samajh.text: Darwaza thodi der khula: kam roshni, kam waqt mein harkat.
samajh.mapping: The open door represents the exposure interval; a moving subject has less time to cross it.
samajh.boundary: Light capture is not literally people walking through a door, and camera motion is a separate cause of blur.

beats.hint: Return to the conditions stated in the comparison.

handbook.markdown: Compare the wheel edge at the same viewing size. Also inspect whether blur is intentional. A faster shutter is a means to an outcome, not a universal improvement.

beats.recap: A way to compare how far the subject moves during the chosen exposure, separately from camera movement.
beats.changeNote: This teaching beat is separate from earlier lesson completion.

beats.title: Change captured light without confusing brightness
beats.outcome: Make a reasoned choice and identify what evidence would change it.
beats.explanation: In a [[photo-m01-light-concept|controlled comparison]], hold scene light and aperture fixed. Halving exposure time halves the light captured. A brighter rendering afterwards does not restore missing captured photons. Inspect the exposure decision and the rendered image separately.

samajh.text: Nal aadhe waqt chale, balti mein kam paani.
samajh.mapping: Time controls the amount accumulated when the flow is unchanged.
samajh.boundary: A sensor is not a bucket; gain, noise and clipping require their own explanation.

beats.hint: Return to the conditions stated in the comparison.

handbook.markdown: Write the controlled conditions before comparing results. If the aperture, illumination or processing changed too, the displayed brightness cannot isolate the shutter-time effect.

extensionCards.prompt: Why does magnifying the image change a sharpness judgment?
extensionCards.answer: A small displacement becomes easier to see at greater magnification.
extensionCards.explanation: Compare candidates at the intended viewing size.
extensionCards.whyItMatters: This optional idea adds a comparison criterion for your next photograph.

extensionCards.prompt: What does panning try to change?
extensionCards.answer: The camera follows the subject so its image moves less relative to the frame.
extensionCards.explanation: The background may streak, and tracking accuracy still matters.
extensionCards.whyItMatters: This optional idea adds a comparison criterion for your next photograph.

extensionCards.prompt: What can a histogram help inspect?
extensionCards.answer: The distribution of rendered tones and possible endpoint clipping.
extensionCards.explanation: It does not by itself show which subject is important or measure every detail of raw sensor exposure.
extensionCards.whyItMatters: This optional idea adds a comparison criterion for your next photograph.

recap.title: Make capture choices: recap
recap.markdown: State the intention, compare a meaningful alternative, then inspect the result. Separate observed differences from your interpretation.

appliedTask.title: Explain two versions of the scene
appliedTask.prompt: Propose two ways to show the cyclist’s motion and explain the capture tradeoff.
appliedTask.modelAnswer: Use a short exposure to emphasize a sharp cyclist or a longer exposure to show movement. At the same aperture and scene light the shorter duration gathers less light. Check motion and brightness separately, and do not claim a tripod freezes the subject.
appliedTask.reasoning: A defensible answer relates the decision to an intention and names a way to compare it.
